.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r4/rules/projects/webdev-task-template: tests/test.sh, tests/tools/score.py, tests/scoring.toml (byte-compared with task: identical), task.toml timeouts, scored/*/judge.toml timeouts and aggregation
evidence: DESIGN (source, supports graded reward): scoring.toml = gates render/constraints 0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floor functional 0.05 (identical to template). score.py:46-48 reward = weighted mean of the three scored dimensions when gates pass and functional > 0.05, so the reward is continuous, not a pass/fail. scored/functional/judge.toml: aggregation = weighted_mean over 43 binary criteria, total weight 58.5; largest single criterion 2.5 (4.3% of functional, 2.6% of reward), smallest 0.5 (0.85%). scored/polish/judge.toml: weighted_mean over 5 binary criteria (weights 3,3,2,1.5,2.5 = 12). scored/visual/judge.toml: weighted_mean over 5 likert criteria, points=5 with anchors 1-5, weight 1.2 each. So there are many independently earnable increments in every scored dimension. One-precondition collapse check (quality-checks.md line 166): functional/prompt.md:13 tells the judge to 'score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures', 'A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row', 'Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles', and to set up again on a fresh job when a setup step fails; polish/prompt.md:12 and visual/prompt.md:32 say the same. The only shared precondition that zeroes a whole dimension is the in-prompt 'Global browser gate' (create job + candidate, Observer sees them in an independent context), which duplicates the constraints gate (gates/constraints/judge.toml:23), so it does not remove spread among apps that already passed the gates. Feature clusters measured by weight share of functional: real-time push (hro_live_board, hro_msg_exchange, hro_unread_counts, hro_unread_scrolled_up, hro_seen) 16.2%; candidate sign-in cluster 9.4%; undo cluster 9.4%; none dominates. Worked spread from the weights: (a) board-only app passing gates with job open, add, add-email rules, one-stage moves, arrive-bottom, reorder only = 6.0/58.5 = 0.103 functional -> above floor, reward ~0.06 + 0.2*visual; (b) full server rules but no live push and no drafts = roughly 0.75-0.8 functional, polish ~0.17-0.33 (live_board/live_thread 6/12 lost), reward ~0.6-0.7; (c) golden-like = near 1. Floor 0.05 needs >2.925 functional weight (e.g. 3 average criteria), which is a low floor and not a binary cliff for partial apps. Plausible broken app that could still score: an app that passes gates but implements no real-time push still earns ~84% of functional mass and half of polish; that is graded, not a discrimination failure. Conforming alternative that could fail: none found that this row's structure would zero as a whole; per-row timing (15 s windows) is a separate fairness question for other rows. MEASUREMENT: raw-evidence-index.json 'scope' says verbatim: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' Its entries are only the scripted golden driver (workspace.cjs, results/workspace.json, server.log, screenshots) and explicitly 'Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, model score or judge-duration measurement.' I did not recompute those artifact hashes because none of them is reward-discrimination evidence. No mutated weak-app reward runs exist, so the claim that the rubric 'produces a spread' is not measured, and REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Runtime and model evidence' requires a hash-bound reward-discrimination record before local clearance. LATENT ALL-OR-NOTHING PATHS (template-controlled, not task defects, but unmeasured): test.sh:224-226 'if ! run_suite scored 11100; then exit 0' leaves the zero reward written at test.sh:60, so if the serial scored suite (functional timeout 9000 + polish 900 + visual 900 = 10800 s with --max-concurrent-agent 1, under the 11100 s outer budget) overruns or rewardkit fails, every app including a strong one gets 0; and the in-prompt Global browser gate means a judge that fails to re-establish the gate observation zeroes functional, which then fails the floor and zeroes the reward. Whether the very long functional protocol (13 protocols, many independent contexts, restart) fits in 9000 s has no full configured timing measurement. These are reasons the spread could collapse in practice and must be measured, not edited (test.sh/score.py/scoring.toml are byte-identical to the template).
counterexample: Not a demonstrated defect. Unmeasured collapse scenario: a strong partial app whose functional judge run exceeds the configured budget (or whose rewardkit scored suite exits non-zero) gets reward 0.0 via test.sh:224-226, the same as a dead app; likewise a judge that fails its own re-run of the in-prompt Global browser gate zeroes functional and the floor zeroes the reward. No run shows whether either happens.
suggested_fix: Obtain the missing evidence rather than editing grading: run the full configured verifier on the golden plus at least two or three mutated weak apps (e.g. no live push; no bulk/undo; board-only) and record hash-bound per-dimension and final rewards showing a graded spread and full-suite durations within budget.
